messages:
Aisha (PM): Heads up — ACME asked for a private pilot with 99th pct latency < 120ms and HSM-backed keys. They want onboarding in 6 weeks. Can we do it? :eyes:
Diego (Eng Runtime): Short answer: tight. Runtime can hit avg <100ms with batching off and KV cache warmed, but 99th at scale needs capacity + prewarm + a fallback plan. Needs infra sloting.
Marta (Infra): We can reserve Dedicated lanes for the pilot but need commit on QPS and request profile. Do we have expected peak QPS and token/sec?
Aisha (PM): ACME expects ~150 QPS peak, mostly short prompts (<=256 tokens). They will send bursts during business hours.
Diego (Eng Runtime): Okay that profile favors lower per-token cost but high tail sensitivity. Recommend: dedicate 2 GPU workers with burst pool and warm prefetch. Also enable prefix cache.
Liam (Security): HSM/KMS for keys — can we do customer-managed keys in their VPC? Private deployment is required. We'll need KMS integration + audit logs. That adds ~1 week for security review and HSM provisioning.
Noah (SRE): If we're spinning Dedicated in their VPC, we need ingress rules and egress policy. Can we reuse the current onramp template? @Marta
Marta (Infra): We can reuse the onramp template but need network CIDR from ACME and an HSM edge. Estimate infra work 10 dev-days for VPC setup + CI for deployment.
Olga (Solutions): Customer will need a short doc on rollout steps and failure modes. Also they asked for canary rollback criteria — they want deterministic failures not silent regressions.
Aisha (PM): Proposal: break pilot into three milestones — (1) infra & security preflight (week 1–2), (2) runtime tuning + canary (week 3–4), (3) validation + SLA handoff (week 5–6). Is that feasible?
Diego (Eng Runtime): With focused effort yes, but we need explicit dev support windows. Also runtime needs model quant variant QA — which model variant are we serving?
Aisha (PM): ACME prefers the v2-large quantized variant we have in catalog. They accept small quality delta for cost.
Diego (Eng Runtime): Good. We'll run a short eval set (200 prompts) to ensure regressions < 2% in top-1 metric. Need a slot for that in week 3.
Liam (Security): I'll start the KMS review today. Please assign me the threat model doc and expected data residency.
Noah (SRE): For capacity, add a prewarm job scheduled 10 minutes before business-hour spikes. Also recommend circuit-breaker policy: if 99th >160ms for 5m, switch traffic to a fallback hosted variant.
Marta (Infra): Resource ask: 2x A100 equiv for dedicated lane, 1x small for canary. I'll put a provisional allocation but need approval from capacity finance.
Aisha (PM): Action items: Diego — eval plan + canary runbook by EOD Wed; Marta — infra estimate + cost by Thu; Liam — KMS review kickoff today; Olga — draft customer runbook and rollback criteria. I'll sync with ACME and propose the milestone dates.
deploy-bot: Scheduled: infra-provisioning-job queued for 2024-05-08T08:00:00Z.
Diego (Eng Runtime): Quick note on fallback: implement a smart fallback that preserves request headers and returns a `x-redwood-fallback` header for observability. Small PR ok if we pair with SRE.
Olga (Solutions): Also include sample incident playbook for longer-than-expected onboarding. ACME legal wants an SLA escalation path.
Aisha (PM): Thanks team. If no major objections I'll mark this as our pilot plan and start calendar invites. :thumbsup:
Noah (SRE): One risk: if ACME spikes to >300 QPS we need autoscale rules tested. Add load test during week 4.
Diego (Eng Runtime): Agree. I'll schedule a 30m run with synthetic bursts.
Liam (Security): Security sign-off contingent on HSM proof-of-possession and audit log retention config — will update by Friday.
Marta (Infra): I'll also validate that Dedicated can attach to ACME's KMS via peered network.
Aisha (PM): Great. I'll capture these in the pilot spec doc and share a link once added. Thanks everyone.
